newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan stocks weaken at start of weekly trade.
newsitem.headline: Jordan stocks weaken at start of weekly trade.

text.p: Low demand kept Jordanian stocks pinned down at start of weekly trade on Saturday but some stocks showed strong individual performance, dealers said.
The official Amman Financial Market 60-share index dropped 0.16 percent, ending the day on 149.25 points in dull 951,268 dinars volume.
After gradual gains earlier this month that sent the market above 150 points last week for the first time in four months, shares ran out of steam in mid-week.
Industrials continued to dominate trade on Saturday.

Market leader Arab Bank, which propelled the index upwards in the first half of September, appeared to lack impetus with none of the large volume witnessed recently. Its stock, the most expensive on the Amman exchange, was unchanged at 241 dinars in low trade worth 43,390 dinars.
"Outside buying was much less than usual and the large volume on Arab Bank was not to be seen," said one broker.
Brokers fear the market may be running out of steam as institutional investors continue to wait in the sidelines and stocks run into profit-taking after the bourse's recent results-driven rally.
Star performer Livestock and Poultry, which has been a focus of investor interest for the fourth week in a row, rose to 0.87 dinars and kept dominating trade with a 252,212 dinar turnover.
Shareholders realising profit on their holdings are feeding the persistent speculative trade on the stock that has seen no fundamentals emerging to otherwise attract investors, dealers said.
Brisk trade triggered mostly by floor traders on Middle East Investment Bank pushed the stock 0.05 dinars to 1.10 with 167,617 shares changing hands.
One of the top gainers, Jordan Phosphate Mines Company, rose 0.09 dinars to 3.210 dinars with 5,100 shares changing hands.
Of 49 stocks traded, 23 fell, 15 advanced, and 11 closed unchanged.
The private Pearl Investable Index of the 45 best performing shares on the exchange fell 0.06 percent to 82.55 points, still 13.57 percent down from the same time last year.
